changes.current_line: Support plans with tiered response times, up to 24/7 coverage.
changes.change: For live-event and peak-moment merchants, especially when the buyer is the COO or ops lead: "A name, not a queue. You get a named solutions engineer and account lead, a direct line, and a clear escalation path. When something breaks, someone who picks up." Do not lead with tiers, response times or SLAs for this buyer. Only add a promise of on-call cover for major events once support and solutions leadership confirm we can staff it.
changes.why: The deciding COO heard our tiered support plans as "a queue with a faster timer", which is the old provider's ticket form, while she was asking "who's my person" and the competitor answered with named people in the room.

changes.current_line: Financial infrastructure to grow globally, in every currency.
changes.change: For live-event and peak-moment merchants whose evaluation was triggered by an outage: don't open with the platform claim (M1), and keep the developer pitch (M2) in the engineering track. Open with what happens when payments fail: "You don't buy uptime, you buy what happens when it's down. Here's who responds in the first four minutes of your on-sale."
changes.why: The switch was triggered by a support response the CEO saw, not by platform capability, and the COO who decided said she buys "what happens when it's down", while our technical proof only landed with the engineers who were not deciding.

changes.change: New proof asset and line for ticketing and live-event buyers: an "On-sale morning plan" that shows on paper who's watching, who you call, and what happens at minute four if payments start failing. Build it with the solutions engineer, give it named contacts, and hand it to the operations decider during the evaluation.
changes.why: The COO explicitly asked to see on paper what we do on an on-sale morning, and we had no such asset and did not build one.

changes.current_line: Trusted by leading businesses; see our customer stories.
changes.change: For ticketing and live-event prospects, back M8 with a person-level reference: a ticketing or live-event customer who will take a call and say who responded during their biggest on-sale. Logos alone are not enough proof for this buyer.
changes.why: The customer asked for a ticketing reference, and the rep says he "had logos" but "didn't have a person", so logo-based proof did not meet the need.
